Use this tool when you need to gather information from multiple related pages across a website or explore a site's structure. attributes.gen_ai.prompt.0.content:
You are a comprehensive financial data collector for Synopsys.
            Collect the full data pack required for a comprehensive briefing.

            Use Tavily together with fetch to gather the requested facts in the order listed. Prefer the most recent data and stop once each section has concrete numbers.

            **REQUIRED DATA TO COLLECT:**
            
            1. **Current Market Data**:
               Search: "Synopsys stock price today current"
               Search: "Synopsys trading volume market data"
               Extract: Current price, daily change ($ and %), trading volume, 52-week range
            
            2. **Latest Earnings Information**:
               Search: "Synopsys latest quarterly earnings results"
               Search: "Synopsys earnings vs estimates beat miss"
               Extract: EPS actual vs estimate, revenue actual vs estimate, beat/miss percentages
            
            3. **Recent Financial News**:
               Search: "Synopsys financial news latest week"
               Search: "Synopsys analyst ratings upgrade downgrade"
               Extract: Provide 5 recent, well-sourced headlines.
            
            4. **Financial Metrics**:
               Search: "Synopsys PE ratio market cap financial metrics"
               Extract: P/E ratio, market cap, key financial ratios
            
            **OUTPUT FORMAT:**
            Organize your findings in these exact sections:
            
            ## CURRENT MARKET DATA
            - Stock Price: $XXX.XX (±X.XX, ±X.X%)
            - Trading Volume: X.X million (vs avg X.X million)
            - 52-Week Range: $XXX.XX - $XXX.XX
            - Market Cap: $XXX billion
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            ## LATEST EARNINGS
            - EPS: $X.XX actual vs $X.XX estimate (beat/miss by X%)
            - Revenue: $XXX billion actual vs $XXX billion estimate (beat/miss by X%)
            - Year-over-Year Growth: X%
            - Quarter: QX YYYY
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            ## RECENT NEWS (Last 7 Days)
            1. [Headline] - [Date] - [Source] - [Impact: Positive/Negative/Neutral]
            2. [Headline] - [Date] - [Source] - [Impact: Positive/Negative/Neutral]
            3. [Continue until you reach the required number of items]
            
            ## KEY FINANCIAL METRICS
            - P/E Ratio: XX.X
            - Market Cap: $XXX billion
            - [Other available metrics]
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            **CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS:**
            - Use EXACT figures, not approximations
            - Include source URLs for verification
            - Note data timestamps/dates
            - If any section is missing data, explicitly state what couldn't be found

attributes.result.structuredContent.results.0.title: Synopsys to cut about 10% of workforce in major restructuring - TradingView
attributes.result.structuredContent.results.0.conte: Synopsys SNPS will lay off about 10% or roughly 2,000 employees, as the chip-design software maker looks to redirect investment towards growth opportunities, according to a regulatory filing on Wednesday. The move comes after the company completed its $35 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of engineering design firm Ansys earlier this year and missed analysts' estimates for third-quarter revenue in September. Synopsys, which had about 20,000 employees as of fiscal 2024-end, expects to incur pre-tax charges to its financial results ranging from $300 million to $350 million. These charges will primarily cover severance and other one-time termination benefits for affected employees, as well as costs associated with certain site closures, the company said. © Copyright Thomson Reuters 2025. ## More news from Reuters

            - Note data timestamps/dates
            - If any section is missing data, explicitly state what couldn't be found

The maker of software used to test and develop chips's stock has dropped by 12.87% in the past month, falling short of the Computer and Technology sector's gain of 2.98% and the S&P 500's gain of 0.95%.

Analysts and investors alike will be keeping a close eye on the performance of Synopsys in its upcoming earnings disclosure. The company's earnings report is set to go public on December 10, 2025. # Synopsys plans 10% job cuts after Ansys deal closure

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)

Synopsys [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/) will lay off about 10% of its workforce, or roughly 2,000 employees, as the chip-design software maker looks to redirect investment towards growth opportunities, according to a regulatory filing on Wednesday.

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)

The move comes after the company completed its $35 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of engineering design firm Ansys earlier this year and missed analysts' estimates for third-quarter revenue in September.

Synopsys said it expects to incur pretax charges to its financial results ranging from $300 million to $350 million, covering severance and other one-time termination benefits, as well as costs associated with certain site closures.

The company said it expects majority of the workforce reductions in the fiscal year 2026 and to substantially complete the restructuring plan by the end of fiscal 2027.

A wave of layoffs has hit global companies this year, with U.S.-based employers cutting more than 150,000 jobs in October , marking the biggest reduction for the month in over 20 years, a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas said last week.

Tech firms led the job cuts in the private sector, followed by retailers and the services sector, the global outplacement company has said.

Synopsys, which counts companies such as Nvidia NVDA.O, Intel [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/) and Qualcomm [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/) among its partners, provides software and hardware used to design advanced processors.

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)

The company has seen a slowdown in China, largely due to new export restrictions disrupting design starts in the country and challenges at a major foundry customer.

In early July, the U.S. lifted restrictions imposed in late May on exports to China for chip design software developers.

# Synopsys plans 10% job cuts after Ansys deal closure

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)

Synopsys [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/) will lay off about 10% of its workforce, or roughly 2,000 employees, as the chip-design software maker looks to redirect investment towards growth opportunities, according to a regulatory filing on Wednesday.

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)

The move comes after the company completed its $35 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of engineering design firm Ansys earlier this year and missed analysts' estimates for third-quarter revenue in September.

Synopsys said it expects to incur pretax charges to its financial results ranging from $300 million to $350 million, covering severance and other one-time termination benefits, as well as costs associated with certain site closures.

The company said it expects majority of the workforce reductions in the fiscal year 2026 and to substantially complete the restructuring plan by the end of fiscal 2027.

A wave of layoffs has hit global companies this year, with U.S.-based employers cutting more than 150,000 jobs in October , marking the biggest reduction for the month in over 20 years, a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas said last week.

Tech firms led the job cuts in the private sector, followed by retailers and the services sector, the global outplacement company has said.

Synopsys, which counts companies such as Nvidia NVDA.O, Intel [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/) and Qualcomm [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/) among its partners, provides software and hardware used to design advanced processors.

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)

The company has seen a slowdown in China, largely due to new export restrictions disrupting design starts in the country and challenges at a major foundry customer.

In early July, the U.S. lifted restrictions imposed in late May on exports to China for chip design software developers.

The maker of software used to test and develop chips's stock has dropped by 12.87% in the past month, falling short of the Computer and Technology sector's gain of 2.98% and the S&P 500's gain of 0.95%.

Analysts and investors alike will be keeping a close eye on the performance of Synopsys in its upcoming earnings disclosure. The company's earnings report is set to go public on December 10, 2025. # Synopsys plans 10% job cuts after Ansys deal closure

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)

Synopsys [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/) will lay off about 10% of its workforce, or roughly 2,000 employees, as the chip-design software maker looks to redirect investment towards growth opportunities, according to a regulatory filing on Wednesday.

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)

The move comes after the company completed its $35 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of engineering design firm Ansys earlier this year and missed analysts' estimates for third-quarter revenue in September.

Synopsys said it expects to incur pretax charges to its financial results ranging from $300 million to $350 million, covering severance and other one-time termination benefits, as well as costs associated with certain site closures.

The company said it expects majority of the workforce reductions in the fiscal year 2026 and to substantially complete the restructuring plan by the end of fiscal 2027.

A wave of layoffs has hit global companies this year, with U.S.-based employers cutting more than 150,000 jobs in October , marking the biggest reduction for the month in over 20 years, a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas said last week.

Tech firms led the job cuts in the private sector, followed by retailers and the services sector, the global outplacement company has said.

Synopsys, which counts companies such as Nvidia NVDA.O, Intel [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/) and Qualcomm [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/) among its partners, provides software and hardware used to design advanced processors.

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)

The company has seen a slowdown in China, largely due to new export restrictions disrupting design starts in the country and challenges at a major foundry customer.

In early July, the U.S. lifted restrictions imposed in late May on exports to China for chip design software developers.

The maker of software used to test and develop chips's stock has dropped by 12.87% in the past month, falling short of the Computer and Technology sector's gain of 2.98% and the S&P 500's gain of 0.95%.

Analysts and investors alike will be keeping a close eye on the performance of Synopsys in its upcoming earnings disclosure. The company's earnings report is set to go public on December 10, 2025. # Synopsys plans 10% job cuts after Ansys deal closure

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)

Synopsys [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/) will lay off about 10% of its workforce, or roughly 2,000 employees, as the chip-design software maker looks to redirect investment towards growth opportunities, according to a regulatory filing on Wednesday.

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)

The move comes after the company completed its $35 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of engineering design firm Ansys earlier this year and missed analysts' estimates for third-quarter revenue in September.

Synopsys said it expects to incur pretax charges to its financial results ranging from $300 million to $350 million, covering severance and other one-time termination benefits, as well as costs associated with certain site closures.

The company said it expects majority of the workforce reductions in the fiscal year 2026 and to substantially complete the restructuring plan by the end of fiscal 2027.

A wave of layoffs has hit global companies this year, with U.S.-based employers cutting more than 150,000 jobs in October , marking the biggest reduction for the month in over 20 years, a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas said last week.

Tech firms led the job cuts in the private sector, followed by retailers and the services sector, the global outplacement company has said.

Synopsys, which counts companies such as Nvidia NVDA.O, Intel [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/) and Qualcomm [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/) among its partners, provides software and hardware used to design advanced processors.

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)

The company has seen a slowdown in China, largely due to new export restrictions disrupting design starts in the country and challenges at a major foundry customer.

In early July, the U.S. lifted restrictions imposed in late May on exports to China for chip design software developers.

# Synopsys plans 10% job cuts after Ansys deal closure

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)

Synopsys [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/) will lay off about 10% of its workforce, or roughly 2,000 employees, as the chip-design software maker looks to redirect investment towards growth opportunities, according to a regulatory filing on Wednesday.

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)

The move comes after the company completed its $35 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of engineering design firm Ansys earlier this year and missed analysts' estimates for third-quarter revenue in September.

Synopsys said it expects to incur pretax charges to its financial results ranging from $300 million to $350 million, covering severance and other one-time termination benefits, as well as costs associated with certain site closures.

The company said it expects majority of the workforce reductions in the fiscal year 2026 and to substantially complete the restructuring plan by the end of fiscal 2027.

A wave of layoffs has hit global companies this year, with U.S.-based employers cutting more than 150,000 jobs in October , marking the biggest reduction for the month in over 20 years, a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas said last week.

Tech firms led the job cuts in the private sector, followed by retailers and the services sector, the global outplacement company has said.

Synopsys, which counts companies such as Nvidia NVDA.O, Intel [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/) and Qualcomm [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/) among its partners, provides software and hardware used to design advanced processors.

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)

The company has seen a slowdown in China, largely due to new export restrictions disrupting design starts in the country and challenges at a major foundry customer.

In early July, the U.S. lifted restrictions imposed in late May on exports to China for chip design software developers.

The stock's performance was behind the S&P 500's daily gain of 0.37%. Meanwhile, the Dow experienced a rise of 0.48%, and the technology-dominated Nasdaq saw an increase of 0.65%.

The maker of software used to test and develop chips's stock has dropped by 12.87% in the past month, falling short of the Computer and Technology sector's gain of 2.98% and the S&P 500's gain of 0.95%.

Analysts and investors alike will be keeping a close eye on the performance of Synopsys in its upcoming earnings disclosure. The company's earnings report is set to go public on December 10, 2025. The company is expected to report EPS of $2.79, down 17.94% from the prior-year quarter. # Synopsys plans 10% job cuts after Ansys deal closure

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)

Synopsys [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/) will lay off about 10% of its workforce, or roughly 2,000 employees, as the chip-design software maker looks to redirect investment towards growth opportunities, according to a regulatory filing on Wednesday.

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)

The move comes after the company completed its $35 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of engineering design firm Ansys earlier this year and missed analysts' estimates for third-quarter revenue in September.

Synopsys said it expects to incur pretax charges to its financial results ranging from $300 million to $350 million, covering severance and other one-time termination benefits, as well as costs associated with certain site closures.

The company said it expects majority of the workforce reductions in the fiscal year 2026 and to substantially complete the restructuring plan by the end of fiscal 2027.

A wave of layoffs has hit global companies this year, with U.S.-based employers cutting more than 150,000 jobs in October , marking the biggest reduction for the month in over 20 years, a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas said last week.

Tech firms led the job cuts in the private sector, followed by retailers and the services sector, the global outplacement company has said.

Synopsys, which counts companies such as Nvidia NVDA.O, Intel [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/) and Qualcomm [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/) among its partners, provides software and hardware used to design advanced processors.

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)

The company has seen a slowdown in China, largely due to new export restrictions disrupting design starts in the country and challenges at a major foundry customer.

In early July, the U.S. lifted restrictions imposed in late May on exports to China for chip design software developers.

The maker of software used to test and develop chips's stock has dropped by 12.87% in the past month, falling short of the Computer and Technology sector's gain of 2.98% and the S&P 500's gain of 0.95%.

# Synopsys plans 10% job cuts after Ansys deal closure

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)

Synopsys [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/) will lay off about 10% of its workforce, or roughly 2,000 employees, as the chip-design software maker looks to redirect investment towards growth opportunities, according to a regulatory filing on Wednesday.

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)

The move comes after the company completed its $35 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of engineering design firm Ansys earlier this year and missed analysts' estimates for third-quarter revenue in September.

Synopsys said it expects to incur pretax charges to its financial results ranging from $300 million to $350 million, covering severance and other one-time termination benefits, as well as costs associated with certain site closures.

The company said it expects majority of the workforce reductions in the fiscal year 2026 and to substantially complete the restructuring plan by the end of fiscal 2027.

A wave of layoffs has hit global companies this year, with U.S.-based employers cutting more than 150,000 jobs in October , marking the biggest reduction for the month in over 20 years, a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas said last week.

Tech firms led the job cuts in the private sector, followed by retailers and the services sector, the global outplacement company has said.

Synopsys, which counts companies such as Nvidia NVDA.O, Intel [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/) and Qualcomm [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/) among its partners, provides software and hardware used to design advanced processors.

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)

The company has seen a slowdown in China, largely due to new export restrictions disrupting design starts in the country and challenges at a major foundry customer.

In early July, the U.S. lifted restrictions imposed in late May on exports to China for chip design software developers.

Synopsys (SNPS) ended the recent trading session at $409.11, demonstrating a -1.74% change from the preceding day's closing price. The stock's performance was behind the S&P 500's daily gain of 0.37%. Meanwhile, the Dow experienced a rise of 0.48%, and the technology-dominated Nasdaq saw an increase of 0.65%.

The maker of software used to test and develop chips's stock has dropped by 12.87% in the past month, falling short of the Computer and Technology sector's gain of 2.98% and the S&P 500's gain of 0.95%.

Analysts and investors alike will be keeping a close eye on the performance of Synopsys in its upcoming earnings disclosure. The company's earnings report is set to go public on December 10, 2025. The company is expected to report EPS of $2.79, down 17.94% from the prior-year quarter. Alongside, our most recent consensus estimate is anticipating revenue of $2.25 billion, indicating a 37.59% upward movement from the same quarter last year.

Regarding the entire year, the Zacks Consensus Estimates forecast earnings of $12.83 per share and revenue of $7.05 billion, indicating changes of -2.8% and 0%, respectively, compared to the previous year.

Investors should also pay attention to any latest changes in analyst estimates for Synopsys. These latest adjustments often mirror the shifting dynamics of short-term business patterns. As such, positive estimate revisions reflect analyst optimism about the business and profitability.

Valuation is also important, so investors should note that Synopsys has a Forward P/E ratio of 29.64 right now. This expresses a premium compared to the average Forward P/E of 28.03 of its industry.

Also, we should mention that SNPS has a PEG ratio of 2.61. This metric is used similarly to the famous P/E ratio, but the PEG ratio also takes into account the stock's expected earnings growth rate. # Synopsys plans 10% job cuts after Ansys deal closure

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)

Synopsys [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/) will lay off about 10% of its workforce, or roughly 2,000 employees, as the chip-design software maker looks to redirect investment towards growth opportunities, according to a regulatory filing on Wednesday.

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/synopsys.svg)

The move comes after the company completed its $35 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of engineering design firm Ansys earlier this year and missed analysts' estimates for third-quarter revenue in September.

Synopsys said it expects to incur pretax charges to its financial results ranging from $300 million to $350 million, covering severance and other one-time termination benefits, as well as costs associated with certain site closures.

The company said it expects majority of the workforce reductions in the fiscal year 2026 and to substantially complete the restructuring plan by the end of fiscal 2027.

A wave of layoffs has hit global companies this year, with U.S.-based employers cutting more than 150,000 jobs in October , marking the biggest reduction for the month in over 20 years, a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas said last week.

Tech firms led the job cuts in the private sector, followed by retailers and the services sector, the global outplacement company has said.

Synopsys, which counts companies such as Nvidia NVDA.O, Intel [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/) and Qualcomm [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/) among its partners, provides software and hardware used to design advanced processors.

![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)
![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/qualcomm.svg)

The company has seen a slowdown in China, largely due to new export restrictions disrupting design starts in the country and challenges at a major foundry customer.

In early July, the U.S. lifted restrictions imposed in late May on exports to China for chip design software developers.

attributes.result.structuredContent.results.0.title: Synopsys to cut about 10% of workforce in major restructuring - TradingView
attributes.result.structuredContent.results.0.conte: Synopsys SNPS will lay off about 10% or roughly 2,000 employees, as the chip-design software maker looks to redirect investment towards growth opportunities, according to a regulatory filing on Wednesday. The move comes after the company completed its $35 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of engineering design firm Ansys earlier this year and missed analysts' estimates for third-quarter revenue in September. Synopsys, which had about 20,000 employees as of fiscal 2024-end, expects to incur pre-tax charges to its financial results ranging from $300 million to $350 million. These charges will primarily cover severance and other one-time termination benefits for affected employees, as well as costs associated with certain site closures, the company said. © Copyright Thomson Reuters 2025. ## More news from Reuters

attributes.result.structuredContent.results.2.title: A ‘tale of two markets’ in private credit emerges as fundamentals diverge – S&P - PitchBook
attributes.result.structuredContent.results.2.conte: ## The downgrade-to-upgrade ratio of borrowers with credit estimates has jumped to 1.8x, the highest since Q2 2024. Many of the strongest private credit borrowers have continued to improve their fundamentals, according to S&P Global Ratings, though pockets of weakness and a growing gap between the best and worst borrowers tell a more nuanced “tale of two markets.” Credit estimates are indications of a likely credit rating on an unrated entity, which S&P provides for some private credit borrowers whose loans are held in CLOs. The downgrade-to-upgrade ratio among borrowers with a credit estimate from the agency jumped to 1.8x, the highest ratio since Q2 2024, according to a Nov. 20 report from S&P.

attributes.result.structuredContent.results.3.conte: "We initiate coverage of Zeta Global with a Buy rating and $26 target price (~+50% upside) as we see it well positioned to capture wallet share in marketing technology, and digital media spend." William Blair upgrades Cognizant Technology Solutions to outperform from market perform William Blair said it's bullish on the technology solutions company. "We are initiating coverage of SiTime, Corp (SITM) with a Buy rating and $350 price target." Raymond James upgrades Doximity to strong buy from outperform The firm said visibility has improved for the software company. "We launch coverage of Certara, the market leader in software modelling for drug development, with a Buy rating and $10 price target, which offers 21% potential upside." Deutsche Bank resumes Carvana as buy Deutsche said the company reminds the firm of Amazon.

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. **Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.
