**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.\\n\\nBut the earnings report a few months ago wasn\u2019t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.\\n\\nOur thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys\u2019s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.\\n\\nSynopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.\\n\\nManagement attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at \u201ca major foundry partner,\u201d which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.\\n\\nAnother key aspect from the quarter is the company\u2019s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.\\n\\nBeyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.\\n\\nBut the earnings report a few months ago wasn\u2019t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.\\n\\nOur thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys\u2019s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.\\n\\nSynopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.\\n\\nManagement attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at \u201ca major foundry partner,\u201d which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.\\n\\nAnother key aspect from the quarter is the company\u2019s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.\\n\\nBeyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

You are a comprehensive financial data collector for Synopsys.
            Collect the full data pack required for a comprehensive briefing.

            Use Tavily together with fetch to gather the requested facts in the order listed. Prefer the most recent data and stop once each section has concrete numbers.

            **REQUIRED DATA TO COLLECT:**
            
            1. **Current Market Data**:
               Search: "Synopsys stock price today current"
               Search: "Synopsys trading volume market data"
               Extract: Current price, daily change ($ and %), trading volume, 52-week range
            
            2. **Latest Earnings Information**:
               Search: "Synopsys latest quarterly earnings results"
               Search: "Synopsys earnings vs estimates beat miss"
               Extract: EPS actual vs estimate, revenue actual vs estimate, beat/miss percentages
            
            3. **Recent Financial News**:
               Search: "Synopsys financial news latest week"
               Search: "Synopsys analyst ratings upgrade downgrade"
               Extract: Provide 5 recent, well-sourced headlines.
            
            4. **Financial Metrics**:
               Search: "Synopsys PE ratio market cap financial metrics"
               Extract: P/E ratio, market cap, key financial ratios
            
            **OUTPUT FORMAT:**
            Organize your findings in these exact sections:
            
            ## CURRENT MARKET DATA
            - Stock Price: $XXX.XX (±X.XX, ±X.X%)
            - Trading Volume: X.X million (vs avg X.X million)
            - 52-Week Range: $XXX.XX - $XXX.XX
            - Market Cap: $XXX billion
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            ## LATEST EARNINGS
            - EPS: $X.XX actual vs $X.XX estimate (beat/miss by X%)
            - Revenue: $XXX billion actual vs $XXX billion estimate (beat/miss by X%)
            - Year-over-Year Growth: X%
            - Quarter: QX YYYY
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            ## RECENT NEWS (Last 7 Days)
            1. [Headline] - [Date] - [Source] - [Impact: Positive/Negative/Neutral]
            2. [Headline] - [Date] - [Source] - [Impact: Positive/Negative/Neutral]
            3. [Continue until you reach the required number of items]
            
            ## KEY FINANCIAL METRICS
            - P/E Ratio: XX.X
            - Market Cap: $XXX billion
            - [Other available metrics]
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            **CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS:**
            - Use EXACT figures, not approximations
            - Include source URLs for verification
            - Note data timestamps/dates
            - If any section is missing data, explicitly state what couldn't be found

Revenue Growth: 8.0% LTM and 9.7% last 3 year average.

 Valuation: SNPS stock trades at a PE multiple of 32.0 [...] SNPS is not immune to significant declines. The downturn in 2018 and the Covid market crash also resulted in declines of approximately 23% and 34%, respectively. Even the inflation impact drove it down nearly 30%. While the stock may possess strong fundamentals, historical trends indicate that sharp downturns are an inevitable part of the experience when markets become unfavorable. [...] After a strong multi-year rally, Synopsys (NASDAQ: SNPS) shares have pulled back in recent months, bringing the stock closer to a key technical support zone. The company, a leader in electronic design automation (EDA) software, has been a consistent performer, benefiting from the growing complexity of semiconductor design and rising demand for AI-driven chips. While short-term sentiment has cooled, the long-term fundamentals remain solid. This pullback could offer investors an attractive entry
attributes.result.structuredContent.results.3.title: Why ORCL, CRM Could Outperform Synopsys Stock - Forbes
attributes.result.structuredContent.results.3.conte: Synopsys (NASDAQ:SNPS) has been a standout performer in the software industry, benefiting from its leadership in electronic design automation (EDA) tools and growing exposure to AI-driven chip development. However, after a strong run-up in recent years, the stock now trades at a premium valuation relative to broader enterprise software peers. At the same time, Oracle (NYSE: ORCL) and Salesforce (NYSE: CRM), both major players in the Application Software space, are delivering faster growth at [...] One approach to ascertain whether Synopsys stock is overpriced compared to other tickers is to evaluate how these metrics compared among companies a year ago. In particular, if there has been a notable reversal in the trend for Synopsys over the past 12 months, there is a possibility that the current disparity may reverse. Conversely, persistent underperformance in revenue and operating income growth for Synopsys would strengthen the conclusion that the stock is overpriced relative to its [...] But do these statistics reveal the entire narrative? Read Buy or Sell SNPS Stock to determine whether Synopsys continues to possess an advantage that can withstand scrutiny. By way of a brief context, Synopsys (SNPS) delivers software for electronic design automation and intellectual property solutions for integrated circuits, facilitating USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, SATA, MIPI, HDMI, and Bluetooth low energy applications.

               Search: "Synopsys latest quarterly earnings results"

               Extract: EPS actual vs estimate, revenue actual vs estimate, beat/miss percentages

               Search: "Synopsys financial news latest week"
               Search: "Synopsys analyst ratings upgrade downgrade"
               Extract: Provide 5 recent, well-sourced headlines.

               Search: "Synopsys PE ratio market cap financial metrics"
               Extract: P/E ratio, market cap, key financial ratios
            
            **OUTPUT FORMAT:**
            Organize your findings in these exact sections:
            
            ## CURRENT MARKET DATA
            - Stock Price: $XXX.XX (±X.XX, ±X.X%)

            - 52-Week Range: $XXX.XX - $XXX.XX
            - Market Cap: $XXX billion
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            ## LATEST EARNINGS
            - EPS: $X.XX actual vs $X.XX estimate (beat/miss by X%)

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

# Synopsys plans 10% job cuts after Ansys deal closure

Refinitiv1 min read

[SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/)[INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/)[QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/)

Synopsys [SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/) will lay off about 10% of its workforce, or roughly 2,000 employees, as the chip-design software maker looks to redirect investment towards growth opportunities, according to a regulatory filing on Wednesday.

The move comes after the company completed its $35 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of engineering design firm Ansys earlier this year and missed analysts' estimates for third-quarter revenue in September.

Synopsys said it expects to incur pretax charges to its financial results ranging from $300 million to $350 million, covering severance and other one-time termination benefits, as well as costs associated with certain site closures.

The company said it expects majority of the workforce reductions in the fiscal year 2026 and to substantially complete the restructuring plan by the end of fiscal 2027.

A wave of layoffs has hit global companies this year, with U.S.-based employers cutting more than 150,000 jobs in October , marking the biggest reduction for the month in over 20 years, a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas said last week.

Tech firms led the job cuts in the private sector, followed by retailers and the services sector, the global outplacement company has said.

Synopsys, which counts companies such as Nvidia NVDA.O, Intel [INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/) and Qualcomm [QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/) among its partners, provides software and hardware used to design advanced processors.

The company has seen a slowdown in China, largely due to new export restrictions disrupting design starts in the country and challenges at a major foundry customer.

In early July, the U.S. lifted restrictions imposed in late May on exports to China for chip design software developers.

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

# Synopsys plans 10% job cuts after Ansys deal closure

Refinitiv1 min read

[SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/)[INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/)[QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/)

Synopsys [SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/) will lay off about 10% of its workforce, or roughly 2,000 employees, as the chip-design software maker looks to redirect investment towards growth opportunities, according to a regulatory filing on Wednesday.

The move comes after the company completed its $35 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of engineering design firm Ansys earlier this year and missed analysts' estimates for third-quarter revenue in September.

Synopsys said it expects to incur pretax charges to its financial results ranging from $300 million to $350 million, covering severance and other one-time termination benefits, as well as costs associated with certain site closures.

The company said it expects majority of the workforce reductions in the fiscal year 2026 and to substantially complete the restructuring plan by the end of fiscal 2027.

A wave of layoffs has hit global companies this year, with U.S.-based employers cutting more than 150,000 jobs in October , marking the biggest reduction for the month in over 20 years, a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas said last week.

Tech firms led the job cuts in the private sector, followed by retailers and the services sector, the global outplacement company has said.

Synopsys, which counts companies such as Nvidia NVDA.O, Intel [INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/) and Qualcomm [QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/) among its partners, provides software and hardware used to design advanced processors.

The company has seen a slowdown in China, largely due to new export restrictions disrupting design starts in the country and challenges at a major foundry customer.

In early July, the U.S. lifted restrictions imposed in late May on exports to China for chip design software developers.

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

# Synopsys plans 10% job cuts after Ansys deal closure

Refinitiv1 min read

[SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/)[INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/)[QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/)

Synopsys [SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/) will lay off about 10% of its workforce, or roughly 2,000 employees, as the chip-design software maker looks to redirect investment towards growth opportunities, according to a regulatory filing on Wednesday.

The move comes after the company completed its $35 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of engineering design firm Ansys earlier this year and missed analysts' estimates for third-quarter revenue in September.

Synopsys said it expects to incur pretax charges to its financial results ranging from $300 million to $350 million, covering severance and other one-time termination benefits, as well as costs associated with certain site closures.

The company said it expects majority of the workforce reductions in the fiscal year 2026 and to substantially complete the restructuring plan by the end of fiscal 2027.

A wave of layoffs has hit global companies this year, with U.S.-based employers cutting more than 150,000 jobs in October , marking the biggest reduction for the month in over 20 years, a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas said last week.

Tech firms led the job cuts in the private sector, followed by retailers and the services sector, the global outplacement company has said.

Synopsys, which counts companies such as Nvidia NVDA.O, Intel [INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/) and Qualcomm [QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/) among its partners, provides software and hardware used to design advanced processors.

The company has seen a slowdown in China, largely due to new export restrictions disrupting design starts in the country and challenges at a major foundry customer.

In early July, the U.S. lifted restrictions imposed in late May on exports to China for chip design software developers.

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

# Synopsys plans 10% job cuts after Ansys deal closure

Refinitiv1 min read

[SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/)[INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/)[QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/)

Synopsys [SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/) will lay off about 10% of its workforce, or roughly 2,000 employees, as the chip-design software maker looks to redirect investment towards growth opportunities, according to a regulatory filing on Wednesday.

The move comes after the company completed its $35 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of engineering design firm Ansys earlier this year and missed analysts' estimates for third-quarter revenue in September.

Synopsys said it expects to incur pretax charges to its financial results ranging from $300 million to $350 million, covering severance and other one-time termination benefits, as well as costs associated with certain site closures.

The company said it expects majority of the workforce reductions in the fiscal year 2026 and to substantially complete the restructuring plan by the end of fiscal 2027.

A wave of layoffs has hit global companies this year, with U.S.-based employers cutting more than 150,000 jobs in October , marking the biggest reduction for the month in over 20 years, a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas said last week.

Tech firms led the job cuts in the private sector, followed by retailers and the services sector, the global outplacement company has said.

Synopsys, which counts companies such as Nvidia NVDA.O, Intel [INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/) and Qualcomm [QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/) among its partners, provides software and hardware used to design advanced processors.

The company has seen a slowdown in China, largely due to new export restrictions disrupting design starts in the country and challenges at a major foundry customer.

In early July, the U.S. lifted restrictions imposed in late May on exports to China for chip design software developers.

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

# Synopsys plans 10% job cuts after Ansys deal closure

Refinitiv1 min read

[SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/)[INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/)[QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/)

Synopsys [SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/) will lay off about 10% of its workforce, or roughly 2,000 employees, as the chip-design software maker looks to redirect investment towards growth opportunities, according to a regulatory filing on Wednesday.

The move comes after the company completed its $35 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of engineering design firm Ansys earlier this year and missed analysts' estimates for third-quarter revenue in September.

Synopsys said it expects to incur pretax charges to its financial results ranging from $300 million to $350 million, covering severance and other one-time termination benefits, as well as costs associated with certain site closures.

The company said it expects majority of the workforce reductions in the fiscal year 2026 and to substantially complete the restructuring plan by the end of fiscal 2027.

A wave of layoffs has hit global companies this year, with U.S.-based employers cutting more than 150,000 jobs in October , marking the biggest reduction for the month in over 20 years, a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas said last week.

Tech firms led the job cuts in the private sector, followed by retailers and the services sector, the global outplacement company has said.

Synopsys, which counts companies such as Nvidia NVDA.O, Intel [INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/) and Qualcomm [QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/) among its partners, provides software and hardware used to design advanced processors.

The company has seen a slowdown in China, largely due to new export restrictions disrupting design starts in the country and challenges at a major foundry customer.

In early July, the U.S. lifted restrictions imposed in late May on exports to China for chip design software developers.

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

# Synopsys plans 10% job cuts after Ansys deal closure

Refinitiv1 min read

[SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/)[INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/)[QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/)

Synopsys [SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/) will lay off about 10% of its workforce, or roughly 2,000 employees, as the chip-design software maker looks to redirect investment towards growth opportunities, according to a regulatory filing on Wednesday.

The move comes after the company completed its $35 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of engineering design firm Ansys earlier this year and missed analysts' estimates for third-quarter revenue in September.

Synopsys said it expects to incur pretax charges to its financial results ranging from $300 million to $350 million, covering severance and other one-time termination benefits, as well as costs associated with certain site closures.

The company said it expects majority of the workforce reductions in the fiscal year 2026 and to substantially complete the restructuring plan by the end of fiscal 2027.

A wave of layoffs has hit global companies this year, with U.S.-based employers cutting more than 150,000 jobs in October , marking the biggest reduction for the month in over 20 years, a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas said last week.

Tech firms led the job cuts in the private sector, followed by retailers and the services sector, the global outplacement company has said.

Synopsys, which counts companies such as Nvidia NVDA.O, Intel [INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/) and Qualcomm [QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/) among its partners, provides software and hardware used to design advanced processors.

The company has seen a slowdown in China, largely due to new export restrictions disrupting design starts in the country and challenges at a major foundry customer.

In early July, the U.S. lifted restrictions imposed in late May on exports to China for chip design software developers.

Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

**Why Synopsys Still Has A Place In Our Portfolio**
---------------------------------------------------

We have owned **Synopsys**[**$SNPS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SNPS/) for several years, viewing it as a foundational business to the entire electronics supply chain. The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.

But the earnings report a few months ago wasn’t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.

Our thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys’s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.

Synopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.

Management attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at “a major foundry partner,” which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.

Another key aspect from the quarter is the company’s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.

Beyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. We’ll monitor this situation carefully to make sure the layoffs aren’t indicative of a deeper company problem during the next earnings update in December.

We own Synopsys and Cadence as an “EDA basket,” treating the two positions as one cohesive whole in our portfolio. This strategy helps us navigate periods of volatility while staying invested in this critical semiconductor sub-industry for the long haul (5+ years).

# Synopsys plans 10% job cuts after Ansys deal closure

Refinitiv1 min read

[SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/)[INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/)[QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/)

Synopsys [SNPS](/symbols/NASDAQ-SNPS/) will lay off about 10% of its workforce, or roughly 2,000 employees, as the chip-design software maker looks to redirect investment towards growth opportunities, according to a regulatory filing on Wednesday.

The move comes after the company completed its $35 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of engineering design firm Ansys earlier this year and missed analysts' estimates for third-quarter revenue in September.

Synopsys said it expects to incur pretax charges to its financial results ranging from $300 million to $350 million, covering severance and other one-time termination benefits, as well as costs associated with certain site closures.

The company said it expects majority of the workforce reductions in the fiscal year 2026 and to substantially complete the restructuring plan by the end of fiscal 2027.

A wave of layoffs has hit global companies this year, with U.S.-based employers cutting more than 150,000 jobs in October , marking the biggest reduction for the month in over 20 years, a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas said last week.

Tech firms led the job cuts in the private sector, followed by retailers and the services sector, the global outplacement company has said.

Synopsys, which counts companies such as Nvidia NVDA.O, Intel [INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/) and Qualcomm [QCOM](/symbols/NASDAQ-QCOM/) among its partners, provides software and hardware used to design advanced processors.

The company has seen a slowdown in China, largely due to new export restrictions disrupting design starts in the country and challenges at a major foundry customer.

In early July, the U.S. lifted restrictions imposed in late May on exports to China for chip design software developers.

The company, along with its peer **Cadence Design Systems**[**$CDNS**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CDNS/), sits at a critical choke point in the semiconductor industry and is essential to secular growth trends, from AI to data centers to auto/industrial markets.\\n\\nBut the earnings report a few months ago wasn\u2019t so great. Sales to China and **Intel**[**$INTC**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/INTC/) knocked Synopsys back by over 30% after Q3 fiscal 2025. And the November selloff has pushed shares even lower, and are now trading at roughly 30x one-year-forward expected earnings.\\n\\nOur thesis is not based on cyclical chip sales, but on the steady, long-term trend of research and development (R&D) spending, which Synopsys\u2019s revenue follows -- as well as Synopsys play on other future tech trends like quantum computing, especially after its acquisition of physics simulation software leader ANSYS.\\n\\nSynopsys has a powerful business model through a combination of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor intellectual property (IP). The last quarter highlighted specific challenges, particularly within the Design IP segment, which was in year-over-year decline.\\n\\nManagement attributed this to a combination of ongoing after-effects from restrictions on Chinese customers, and headwinds at \u201ca major foundry partner,\u201d which can be easily inferred as Intel. In response, Synopsys is pivoting its IP roadmap to concentrate on higher-growth opportunities, including an increased focus on customized IP. Layoffs of 10% of its global workforce was also announced as ANSYS overlap expenses are being cut.\\n\\nAnother key aspect from the quarter is the company\u2019s free cash flow (FCF) cycle. While peer Cadence appears to have already hit a positive inflection point, we are still awaiting this turnaround for Synopsys. This delayed FCF recovery, paired with the stock's premium valuation, explains the market's discomfort and the resulting volatility when short-term results don't perfectly align with expectations.\\n\\nBeyond revenue growth, a key part of our thesis is long-term profit margin expansion. With the ANSYS acquisition now complete, the margin expansion story can continue. Synopsys, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------

Synopsys, Inc. provides electronic design automation software products used to design and test integrated circuits. It operates in two segments, Design Automation and Design IP. The company offers Digital and Custom IC Design solution that provides digital design implementation solutions; Verification solution that offers virtual prototyping, static and formal verification, simulation, emulation, field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based prototyping, and debug solutions; FPGA design products that are programmed to perform specific functions; synopsys technology computer-aided design (TCAD), mask synthesis, and manufacturing analytic solutions; and AI-driven EDA solutions. It also provides intellectual property (IP) solutions for UCIe, USB, PCI Express, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, and HDMI; logic libraries and embedded memories; processor cores, software, and application-specific instruction-set processor tools for embedded applications; security IP solutions; IP solutions for automotive market; and system-on-chip (SoC) infrastructure IP, datapath and building block IP, and verification IP products, as well as mathematical and floating-point components, and Arm AMBA interconnect fabric and peripherals. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.
